title: Grammar Path
description: Canonical teaching and assessment source for grammar targets that connect the book course with the site's extended grammar material.

targets.title: Gender and number agreement
targets.summary: Match an adjective to a masculine singular, feminine singular, or plural noun.
targets.rule: The adjective normally follows the noun and changes with it: masculine singular, feminine singular, or plural.
targets.pattern: ktieb ġdid | karozza ġdida | kotba ġodda
targets.commonMistake: Do not reuse the masculine singular adjective after a feminine or plural noun.
targets.masteryLabel: choose and produce the adjective form that agrees with its noun

recognition.prompt: Which phrase has correct feminine agreement?
recognition.explanation: Karozza is feminine singular, so aħmar changes to ħamra.

production.prompt: Complete the plural adjective: Il-kotba huma _____. (The books are new.)
production.explanation: The plural noun kotba takes the plural adjective ġodda.

targets.title: Near and far demonstratives
targets.summary: Choose demonstratives by distance, gender, and number.
targets.rule: Use dan, din, dawn for things that are near and dak, dik, dawk for things that are farther away.
targets.pattern: dan/dak + masculine | din/dik + feminine | dawn/dawk + plural
targets.commonMistake: Distance is not the only choice: singular demonstratives must also agree with the noun's gender.
targets.masteryLabel: select a near or far demonstrative with the correct gender and number

recognition.explanation: Karozza is feminine singular, so the near demonstrative is din.

production.prompt: Complete with a near plural demonstrative: _____ il-kotba huma ġodda.
production.explanation: Dawn is used for plural things that are near.

targets.title: Possession with għandu
targets.summary: Use the complete għandu paradigm to say who has something.
targets.rule: The form changes with the possessor: għandi, għandek, għandu, għandha, għandna, għandkom, għandhom.
targets.commonMistake: Choose the form from the owner, not from the gender or number of the possessed object.
targets.masteryLabel: choose and produce the correct għandu form for the possessor

recognition.prompt: Which sentence correctly says “We have a book”?

production.prompt: Complete the possession form: Huma _____ karozza.

targets.title: Definite article and assimilation
targets.summary: Apply il-, l-, or an assimilated article before a noun.
targets.rule: Use il- before most consonants, l- before vowels and għ or h, and repeat the first sound with ċ, d, n, r, s, t, x, z, or ż.
targets.commonMistake: Do not keep il- unchanged before a consonant that requires assimilation.
targets.masteryLabel: apply the regular, reduced, or assimilated definite article

recognition.explanation: Before d, the article assimilates and becomes id-.

production.prompt: Complete the article: _____ tinsab ħdejn l-iskola. (The house is near the school.)
production.explanation: Dar takes the assimilated article id-.

targets.title: Numbers 11–19 with -il
targets.sourceRequirement: Numbers 11–19 with -il and a singular noun
targets.summary: Connect the numbers 11–19 to a counted singular noun with -il.
targets.rule: Before a counted noun, the numbers 11–19 take -il and the noun stays singular.
targets.commonMistake: Do not omit -il or change the counted noun to a plural form in this pattern.
targets.masteryLabel: connect 11–19 to a singular counted noun with -il

recognition.explanation: The number takes -il and the counted noun remains singular.

production.prompt: Complete the number phrase: Hemm _____ student fil-klassi. (There are fifteen students.)
production.explanation: Use ħmistax-il before the singular counted noun student.

targets.title: Future with se
targets.sourceRequirement: Future with se plus a present-type verb form
targets.summary: Build a future plan with se and the present-type form that matches the subject.
targets.rule: Place se before the present-type verb form; keep the person marking on the verb.
targets.pattern: jien se mmur | hi se tilgħab | aħna se naraw
targets.commonMistake: Do not put se before a past-tense form such as mort when describing a future plan.

examples.english: Tomorrow I will go to the city.

targets.masteryLabel: choose and produce se with the correct present-type verb form

recognition.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes a future plan?
recognition.explanation: Use se before the matching present-type form mmur.

production.prompt: Complete the future plan: Għada _____ il-baħar. (Tomorrow I will go to the seaside.)
production.explanation: The future phrase is se plus the first-person form mmur.

targets.title: Can, must, want, and need
targets.summary: Use common modal patterns before an action to express ability, obligation, preference, or need.
targets.rule: Use a modal expression such as nista', irrid, nixtieq, or għandi bżonn before the action form.
targets.pattern: nista' mmur | irrid naħdem | nixtieq nixrob | għandi bżonn nistrieħ
targets.commonMistake: Keep the action after the modal instead of translating the English pattern word by word.

examples.english: I would like to drink coffee.

targets.masteryLabel: select and produce a modal expression before an action

recognition.prompt: Which sentence politely says “I would like to drink coffee”?
recognition.explanation: Nixtieq followed by the action expresses a polite preference.

production.prompt: Complete the need pattern: _____ nistrieħ. (I need to rest.)
production.explanation: Għandi bżonn before an action expresses need.

targets.title: Subject pronouns
targets.summary: Choose the subject pronoun that matches the person and number of the sentence.
targets.rule: Use jien, inti, hu, hi, aħna, intom, and huma for I, you singular, he, she, we, you plural, and they.
targets.pattern: jien | inti | hu/hi | aħna | intom | huma
targets.commonMistake: Do not confuse inti with intom: inti addresses one person and intom addresses more than one.
targets.masteryLabel: choose and produce the subject pronoun for person and number

recognition.explanation: Aħna is the first-person plural subject pronoun.

production.prompt: Complete with the subject pronoun: _____ noqogħdu Malta. (We live in Malta.)
production.explanation: Aħna is used when the subject is we.

targets.title: Present-tense person forms
targets.summary: Match a present-tense verb form to its subject pronoun.
targets.rule: Present forms mark the person with a prefix and sometimes a plural ending; learn each verb as a complete pronoun pattern.
targets.pattern: jien niekol | inti tiekol | hu jiekol | aħna nieklu | intom tieklu | huma jieklu
targets.commonMistake: Do not keep the same present form for every pronoun; both the prefix and the plural ending may change.
targets.masteryLabel: select and produce a present form that matches its subject

recognition.prompt: Which sentence correctly means "She eats bread"?
recognition.explanation: The third-person feminine present form is tiekol.

production.prompt: Complete the present form: Aħna _____ l-ħobż. (We eat bread.)
production.explanation: The aħna form of kiel in the present is nieklu.

targets.title: Question patterns
targets.summary: Build information questions with a question word and yes-no questions with the matching verb form.
targets.rule: Place a question word such as min, x', fejn, meta, għaliex, or kif before the rest of the question; a yes-no question can begin directly with the person-marked verb.
targets.commonMistake: Keep the verb matched to the person being asked; a question word does not replace the verb.

examples.english: What do you do in the evening?

targets.masteryLabel: choose and produce a question word with the correct verb form

recognition.prompt: Which question asks where someone lives?

production.prompt: Complete the place question: _____ toqgħod? (Where do you live?)
production.explanation: Fejn is the question word for where.

targets.title: Basic sentence order
targets.summary: Build a clear statement from a subject, a person-marked verb, and its object, place, or time phrase.
targets.rule: A safe beginner pattern is subject plus matching verb plus the remaining information; a time or place phrase can move to the front for emphasis.
targets.pattern: Jien naqra ktieb. | Hi tgħix Malta. | Filgħodu nixrob it-te.
targets.commonMistake: Do not separate a verb from a required object or reuse an English auxiliary such as do in a Maltese statement.

examples.english: In the morning I drink tea.

targets.masteryLabel: recognize and produce a complete basic Maltese statement

recognition.prompt: Which option is a complete basic statement?
recognition.explanation: The safe beginner order is subject, matching verb, then object.

production.prompt: Complete the statement: Jien _____ ktieb kull filgħaxija. (I read a book every evening.)
production.explanation: Naqra is the first-person present form and comes before its object.

targets.title: Collective, unit, and plural forms
targets.sourceRequirement: Unit, collective, and plural food nouns
targets.summary: Distinguish a collective food noun from one countable unit and from several separate units.
targets.rule: Many food nouns use a collective base for the substance or crop, a singulative form for one item, and a separate plural for countable items; learn the three forms together.
targets.commonMistake: Do not use the collective form when the sentence explicitly counts one separate item.
targets.masteryLabel: choose and produce the collective, unit, or plural noun form

recognition.explanation: Tuffieħa is the singulative form for one apple.

production.prompt: Complete with one countable item: Għandi _____ waħda. (I have one apple.)
production.explanation: Use the singulative form tuffieħa for one item.

targets.title: Past-tense person forms
targets.summary: Match a completed past action to the ending required by its subject.
targets.rule: Past forms commonly mark the person with an ending; learn the whole paradigm because the verb stem may also change.
targets.pattern: jien mort | hu mar | hi marret | aħna morna | intom mortu | huma marru
targets.commonMistake: Do not place a present prefix on a past form or use the third-person masculine form for every subject.
targets.masteryLabel: select and produce a past form that matches its subject

recognition.prompt: Which sentence correctly means "She went to school"?
recognition.explanation: The third-person feminine past form is marret.

production.prompt: Complete the past form: Huma _____ il-belt ilbieraħ. (They went to the city yesterday.)
production.explanation: The huma past form of mar is marru.

targets.title: Verb negation with ma...x
targets.sourceRequirement: Negative verb pattern with ma and -x
targets.summary: Negate a person-marked verb by placing ma before it and attaching -x to the verb form.
targets.rule: The standard verb negative surrounds the conjugated form: ma plus verb plus -x.
targets.pattern: ma nħobbx | ma niekolx | ma mmurx
targets.commonMistake: Do not omit either half of the negative pattern, and attach -x to the verb rather than writing it as a separate word.

examples.english: Today I am not going to the city.

targets.masteryLabel: recognize and produce the complete ma...x negative pattern

recognition.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "I do not like coffee"?
recognition.explanation: The verb is surrounded by ma and the attached ending -x.

production.prompt: Complete the negative: Jien _____ il-kafè. (I do not like coffee.)
production.explanation: The complete negative form is ma nħobbx.

targets.title: Singular and plural imperative
targets.summary: Choose a command form according to whether it addresses one person or more than one.
targets.rule: Use the singular imperative for one addressee and the corresponding plural imperative for a group; many plural commands end in -u.
targets.commonMistake: Do not add a subject pronoun to a basic command, and do not use the singular command for a group.
targets.masteryLabel: select and produce a singular or plural imperative for the addressee

recognition.prompt: Which command tells a group to open the books?
recognition.explanation: Iftħu is the plural imperative used for more than one addressee.

production.prompt: Complete the plural command: _____ l-kotba. (Open the books.)
production.explanation: Use the plural imperative Iftħu when speaking to a group.

targets.title: Preposition and article contractions
targets.sourceRequirement: Place prepositions with the definite article
targets.summary: Combine the place preposition fi with the following definite article.
targets.rule: Before a definite noun, fi contracts with the article while preserving its regular, reduced, or assimilated sound.
targets.pattern: fi + il-kamra = fil-kamra | fi + id-dar = fid-dar | fi + l-iskola = fl-iskola
targets.commonMistake: Do not leave fi and the definite article as two unchanged words when a contraction is required.

examples.english: The table is in the room.
The children are in the house.

targets.masteryLabel: recognize and produce fi contracted with the definite article

recognition.prompt: Which phrase correctly means "in the house"?
recognition.explanation: Fi contracts with the assimilated article id- to form fid-.

production.prompt: Complete the place phrase: Il-ktieb qiegħed _____ borża. (The book is in the bag.)
production.explanation: Fi plus il-borża contracts to fil-borża.

targets.title: Comparatives with minn
targets.summary: Compare two people, objects, places, or conditions with a comparative and minn.
targets.rule: Put the comparative after the first item and introduce the second item with minn, which may combine with an article.
targets.commonMistake: Do not omit minn when both sides of the comparison are stated.

examples.english: This house is bigger than that one.
My room is smaller than yours.

examples.maltese: Illum hemm inqas riħ minn ieri.
examples.english: Today there is less wind than yesterday.

targets.masteryLabel: recognize and produce a complete comparison with minn

recognition.prompt: Which sentence makes a complete comparison?
recognition.explanation: The second item in a full comparison is introduced by minn.

production.prompt: Complete the comparison: Il-kamra tiegħi _____ minn tiegħek. (My room is smaller than yours.)
production.explanation: Iżgħar means smaller and is followed here by minn.
